title: Every contents-API write lands on the default branch
description:
Every write the factory makes through the contents API lands on the repository's DEFAULT branch, whatever ref the store was built for.

Observed after run_ba1cc951cd184126b7c9e3c54fecc5c2 (epic uzc, integration branch epic/uzc):

    origin/main      41804637 ticfac run run_ba1cc951...: open the run state
                     5d3c6591 ticfac run run_ba1cc951...: record attempt 1 of f8l
                     f0d0bb76 tick f8l: tracker update by the run reconciler
    origin/epic/uzc  43490a23  <- untouched, exactly where the run cut it

Mechanism: GitHub's contents API takes the target ref DIFFERENTLY for reads and writes. A read takes ?ref=<branch> in the query string. A write takes a `branch` field IN THE BODY, and when it is absent GitHub commits to the repository's default branch - the query string is not consulted.

cloudflare/src/git-contents.ts builds one URL for both:

    const entryURL = (path) => `${base}/repos/${project}/contents/${path}?ref=${encodeURIComponent(ref)}`;

and put() sends a body with no branch:

    async create(path, input) {
      return put(path, { message: input.message, content: base64Utf8(input.content) });
    }

So reads are correct and writes silently go somewhere else. Nothing errors: GitHub accepts the write and answers 201, and the store reports `written` with a commit sha - on the wrong branch.

Why this is serious beyond the misplaced files:

1. It writes to the DEFAULT branch directly. .tick/config.md declares "Epic integration goes through a PR + CI gate ... No direct merges of epic branches to the default branch. The merge itself is a person's." A cloud run currently commits to main with no PR, no CI and no person.
2. The run's own durable state diverges from the branch it reads. The reconciler reads the tracker and its checkpoint from epic/<epic> and writes them to main, so on the next pass it cannot see what it just wrote - which is also a candidate explanation for the "checkpoint conflict: ... already exists" error seen on the same run.
3. It is invisible. The write succeeds, so nothing in the feed, the evidence or the tests says a word.

Fix: send `branch` in the body of every contents write (create and update), from the same ref the store was constructed with. While there, check every other GitHub write path in the bundle for the same shape - tracker-write.ts is the other consumer of this mechanism.

A guard is worth having, and it must assert the REQUEST, not the response: a test that captures the PUT body and refuses one whose branch is missing or is not the store's ref. A test that only checks the store's answer passes today.

Found by performing u9h: the run wrote to main and I noticed only because `git pull` in the ticks checkout brought its commits down.
acceptance_criteria: A write through the contents store commits to the store's own ref, proven by a test that captures the PUT body and refuses a missing or wrong branch field; no cloud run writes to the default branch
closed_reason: Landed via PR #23: every contents write carries branch from the store's ref. GitHub takes the ref in the query on a read and in the body on a write; the query is ignored on PUT, so every write went to the default branch with a 201. Stray commits reverted in ticks a58105db.
